n: The Gods resolve to complete the heavens, the earth, and everything in them. Chapter 4 was largely the plan; now it will be carried out.

f.g: multitudes — all the beings and things that fill the heavens and earth.

f.w: finish the heavens and the earth

n: The Gods agree to end their counseled work on the seventh time and to rest from it.
The Gods set apart the seventh time as holy, as part of their council’s decisions. The Sabbath is rooted in the pattern of creation itself.

f.g: made holy, set apart for God.

n: The Gods now come down and actually form the heavens and the earth, bringing about what they had planned.

f.g: here, the origins or history of the heavens and earth.

f.w: the Gods came down and formed

n: Everything was done exactly as previously counseled — every plant planned before it grew. No rain had yet fallen, and there was no man to till the ground.

f.w: before it was in the earth

n: Instead of rain, a mist rose from the earth and watered the ground — preparing it for life.
The Gods form man’s body from the dust and place his preexisting spirit into it, breathing life into him. Abraham uniquely clarifies that the man’s spirit was put into the body.

f.w: took his spirit (that is, the man's spirit), and put it into him

n: The Gods plant a garden eastward in Eden and place the man there. The man is described as a spirit placed in a formed body.
The garden grows beautiful and fruitful trees, including the tree of life and the tree of knowledge of good and evil — the two trees at the center of the Fall story.

f.w: the tree of knowledge of good and evil

n: A river flows out of Eden to water the garden and then divides into four branches.

f.g: four headwaters or branches; Genesis 2:11-14 names them.

n: Man is placed in Eden to care for and guard it. Work and stewardship were part of God’s plan from the start.

f.w: to dress it and to keep it

n: The Gods give man freedom to eat of every tree in the garden — a generous permission before the one restriction.

Only the tree of knowledge is forbidden, with the warning of death. Abraham adds that the “day” of death followed the Lord’s time — Kolob’s reckoning of a thousand years — since Adam had not yet been given earthly time.
The Gods declare it is not good for man to be alone and plan to make a “help meet” — a fitting partner for him.

f.g: a helper suited to him; Hebrew ‘ezer kenegdo, “a help corresponding to him.” ‘Ezer is also used of God (Psalms 33:20).

n: Adam is put into a deep sleep, and a rib is taken from his side. The image suggests a partner who stands beside him.
From the rib the Gods form a woman and bring her to the man. God Himself introduces the first marriage.
Adam recognizes her as part of himself — “bone of my bones” — and calls her Woman because she came from man.
This is the foundation of marriage: a man leaves his parents and holds fast to his wife, and they become one. Jesus later quoted this verse.
Adam and Eve are naked and unashamed — a picture of innocence before the Fall.
The Gods form the animals and bring them to Adam to name. Naming them shows Adam’s God-given stewardship and understanding.

f.w: to see what he would call them

n: Adam names all the animals, and for him a fitting partner was found — Eve, who would join him in God’s plan.
